messages:
maya: Heads-up: ap-sg dedicated pool is hitting sustained admission failures — 429s and queue growth. Not spikes, it's a plateau: ~85% GPU util + long queues. Anyone picking this up?

devon: On it. Seeing `admit_rejects` counter climbing in metrics. Fairshare evictions are up. Is autoscale disabled for that pool? :thinking_face:

sre-alex: Investigating. `kubectl get pods -n dedicated-ap-sg` shows nodes Ready but two nodes reporting GPU memory pressure. Pulling admission-controller logs now.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1871000123. Pager notified. Runbook v2: https://internal/runbooks/dedicated-admit

liam: Any noisy tenants? I can pull tenant histograms.

maya: Tenant histogram shows three tenants spiking tail latency: cust-alpha, cust-beta, cust-gamma. cust-alpha started a ramp at ~07:10 UTC with very long sequences.

devon: Temporary mitigation options: bump enterprise fairshare weight (fast) or enable spillover to hosted for non-sensitive tenants (safer but requires routing changes). Thoughts?

sre-alex: Quick patch applied: admission override to prioritize enterprise commits. Command: `PATCH /admission/pools/ap-sg -> {"priority_overrides": ["enterprise"]}`. Watching metrics.

maya: If we do that, we need to communicate to affected tenants. Also can we enable burst autoscale? Current policy min=3 max=10 but burst/autoscale disabled due to billing caps on the org.

devon: I pushed the override. admit_rejects dropped from ~142/min to ~22/min within 6m. Queue length down from ~430 -> ~120. :thumbsup: Note: this will increase GPU hours if we let it run.

liam: Found misconfigured scheduled batch for cust-gamma: single requests with >50k tokens earlier. That's pushing KV cache and holding slots for long time. Killed a few lanes.

sre-alex: We should enforce ingress sequence-length limits for dedicated pools and route overlong requests to a batch/async queue with different QoS. Proposed cap: 16k tokens, with a helpful 429 body suggesting hosted fallback or chunking.

maya: Agree. Opened PR to add token cap + improved 429 payload linking hosted fallback docs. Also adding tenant-level rate-shed rules for long-seq.

devon: Quick log excerpt from admission-controller (errors repeating):
``` 
I0317 07:12:08 admission.go:214] admit_reject tenant=cust-alpha reason=capacity_exhausted queue_len=512
I0317 07:12:09 admission.go:214] admit_reject tenant=cust-alpha reason=sequence_too_long len=51200
```

sre-alex: Notes: nodes are Ready but we saw uneven placement; two nodes had <5% free GPU memory causing OOM eviction attempts in the serving containers. Scheduler placed a 2.3TB model shard heavy tenant on busy nodes. Need to improve placement affinity for long-seq workloads.

ops-bot: Cost alert posted: estimated extra GPU-hours for ap-sg during incident: 9.2h. Billing notified.

liam: Short-term runbook items: 1) keep enterprise override until queues stable, 2) disable scheduled batch for cust-gamma until they adjust payloads, 3) enable spillover routing for best-effort tenants.

maya: Long-term: autoscale policy review (raise commit cap or dynamic burst budget), admission-controller backpressure improvements, tenant QoS docs + enforcement, placement affinity change for long-seq model shards. I'll draft the postmortem.

devon: Also recommend a per-tenant token cap soft-fail that returns a clear error and offers chunking helper links.

sre-alex: Follow-up tasks assigned in the incident ticket. I'll take placement affinity and scheduler change.

maya: Thanks all. I'll start the postmortem draft and loop in support for customer comms. Close when remediation PRs merged.

liam: thx, closing my ops actions.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1871000123 marked "stabilized" at 1871000420.

maya: Closing thread, will update postmortem link once ready. :white_check_mark:
